Possible cause and reproducer:
1) Start partition eviction
2) Force kill node (kill -9) after partition file truncate
3) Start node again and iterate over index

The main problem that file truncation is not synchronized with actual checkpoint which can lead to the situation, that after crash recovery we have links in index tree to the data pages which were already removed during file truncation.
One of the possible solutions is to mark such partition files for deletion and safely truncate them on the next checkpoint.

This mechanism can be ressurected from ignite-2.0.2.b1 branch.
See

Jokser,

A few comments:
1) I think this piece of code

            newTag = pageMemory.invalidate(grp.groupId(), partId);

            if (grp.walEnabled())
                ctx.wal().log(new PartitionDestroyRecord(grp.groupId(), partId));

should be moved from destroyCacheDataStore0 to the place where we run the actual file truncation because partition destroy record should be logged together with file truncation
2) On replay, we should similarly invoke invalidate(...) instead of clearAsync - the latter method was introduced before we have an O(1) invalidate method
3) I think there is a race in cancelOrWaitPartitionDestroy: we first check curCpProgress, then we use lock to access the scheduledCp, but a concurrent thread may have switched these fields in between two reads. I think both fields should be read inside a single synchronized block
4) Please carefully check that there are no deadlocks on TC because we added a synchronous cancelOrWaitPartitionDestroy in createCacheDataStore0
agoncharuk Concerns have fixed, crash recovery has been reworked. Could you please review the fix again?
